trips.title: Istria: The Parenzana & the Hilltowns
trips.summary: The Parenzana is an abandoned narrow-gauge railway that ran 123 km from Trieste to Poreč between 1902 and 1935, and its Croatian section is now the best-surfaced long gravel corridor in the northern Adriatic. This week uses it as a spine: hardpack embankments, unlit stone tunnels and viaducts through the Mirna valley, with detours climbing off it to Grožnjan, Motovun, Buje and Oprtalj, each a walled hilltown on its own knoll. Add a truffle lunch in Livade, two days of Malvazija tasting, an optional 1,401 m ascent of Vojak on Učka, and a finish on the Rovinj coast. It is the gentlest week in this collection on paper and the most tempting to overcook, because every hilltown demands a climb.

trips.title: Peloponnese: Arcadia & the Argolid
trips.summary: The Peloponnese hides its cycling behind its archaeology. Behind Nafplio's Venetian waterfront and the theatre at Epidaurus sits Arcadia, a highland of stone villages, plane-shaded ravines and roads that switchback for twenty kilometres without a village. This week works three distinct terrains: the Argolid's low, fast, ruin-studded coastal plain; the Lousios gorge country around Dimitsana and Stemnitsa, where monasteries are built into cliff faces; and the eastern seaboard at Leonidio, where 300 m orange limestone walls rise straight out of a village and the road to Kosmas is one of the great climbs of southern Europe. It rewards riders who accept rough chip-seal, long empty stretches and a genuine language barrier once you leave the coast.

trips.title: The Balaton Ring: Seven Days Around Hungary's Inland Sea
trips.summary: Balaton is shallow, jade-green and 77 km long, and the ring around it is flat enough that all the climbing is voluntary. This week rides the paved Balatoni Bringakör anticlockwise, then leaves it twice, over the…

trips.title: Valle d'Itria & Salento by Bike
trips.summary: The Valle d'Itria is a shallow limestone basin stitched with dry-stone walls, olive trunks the width of a car, and trulli that appear in fields the way boulders do elsewhere. Riding it means constant micro-climbs on white lanes between Locorotondo, Cisternino and Martina Franca, then a fast drop off the Murgia escarpment at Ostuni to a coastline of dune, macchia and Roman ruin. The last two days shift south to the Salento, where the landscape flattens, the light hardens, and the ride from Lecce to Otranto runs through baroque towns and scarred olive groves. It is a cycling week built around food and surface variety rather than climbing, and it rewards a gravel bike over a race bike.

trips.title: Luxembourg on the PC Network
trips.summary: A week on Luxembourg's national PC cycle routes, linking the Moselle vineyards to the Mullerthal sandstone and the Our valley, with free public transport throughout.

trips.sub: Codru hills, Strășeni, Nisporeni, Călărași, Orhei
trips.summary: The Codru is not flat and Moldova is not a road-bike country. This is 370 km of ridge-and-valley on a 35-40 mm tyre: resurfaced asphalt for an hour, then a slab of cracked Soviet concrete, then eight kilometres of…

trips.title: Kotor Serpentine & Lovćen: 25 Hairpins Above the Boka
trips.sub: Bay of Kotor, Lovćen NP & the Old Royal Capital
trips.summary: This is a week built around one road. The old Austro-Hungarian carriage road from Kotor to Njeguši, the P1, the Kotor Serpentine, the Ladder of Cattaro's tarmac successor, stacks twenty-five numbered hairpins into a limestone wall and lifts you from the quay to a saddle at nearly 950 m without a single flat metre. Everything else in the week is arranged around that climb: a bay warm-up on the Perast-Risan shore, the high plateau of Lovćen NP and Njegoš's mausoleum, the imperial small-town calm of Cetinje, a gravel day into the Krivošije backcountry, a Vrmac ridge traverse, and a coastal spin down the Budva riviera. It suits climbers who are comfortable descending on narrow roads with hip-height stone parapets and, sometimes, none.

trips.title: Frisian Dikes and the Wadden Coast
trips.summary: A week along the Waddenzee sea dikes of Friesland and Groningen on EuroVelo 12, with two days on Ameland and the terp villages inland.

trips.title: The Waterline Ride from Amsterdam to Kinderdijk
trips.summary: Amsterdam to Kinderdijk by knooppunten and the Waterlinieroute, following the UNESCO-listed Dutch Water Defence Lines through forts, dikes and river ferries.

trips.title: Green Velo Through Podlasie: Marsh, Forest and the Eastern Trail
trips.sub: Podlaskie, Puszcza Knyszyńska, Narew & Biebrza valleys, Puszcza Białowieska
trips.summary: Podlasie is the flattest, emptiest and least-visited corner of Poland, and the Green Velo runs straight through the middle of it. Seven days of near-zero gradient, wooden Orthodox churches, storks on every second…

trips.title: Alentejo & Costa Vicentina Gravel
trips.summary: The Alentejo is Europe's emptiest agricultural landscape and its gravel is correspondingly generous, hundreds of kilometres of hard clay and schist farm track winding through montado, the cork-oak savannah that has been managed the same way for eight centuries. This week runs from Évora's Roman and Manueline core east to the walled hilltop of Monsaraz above the Alqueva reservoir, south through Mértola's Islamic castle to the Guadiana, then west to the Atlantic, where the Costa Vicentina delivers cliffs, storks nesting on sea stacks, and a headwind that defines the last two days. It is a route about space, silence and heat management rather than climbing, and it needs a rider comfortable being 30 km from the nearest café.

trips.summary: Slovakia has one finished long-distance cycle route and one that is half-built, and this week rides both honestly. The Danube dyke below Bratislava is flat, smooth asphalt across Europe's largest river island, with a…

trips.title: Soča Valley & Goriška Brda Gravel Week
trips.summary: Two textures in one week. The first half climbs repeatedly out of Kobarid onto the Kolovrat ridge, a militarised limestone spine where Isonzo Front trenches still cut the grass and tarmac gives way to white dolomite without warning. The second half drops 900 m into Goriška Brda, where gradients shorten but never stop, hills are terraced in ribolla gialla, and the Italian border is a line you cross four times a day. It suits riders who like climbing in 6-14 km doses on 40-45 mm tyres. Distances stay at 55-80 km because the ascent-per-kilometre ratio is punishing.

trips.title: Girona & the Costa Brava
trips.summary: Girona is not a scenic backdrop that happens to have cyclists in it; it is a town whose economy has partly reorganised around them. Within 20 km of the Pont de Pedra you can be on the Els Àngels climb, on the hardpack of the Ruta del Carrilet, or in the Gavarres forest on gravel that has never seen a car. This week strings together the four climbs that define the local calendar, Els Àngels, Rocacorba, Sant Hilari and Sant Grau, connects them with the two greenways that make recovery days genuinely restful, and puts one day on the Costa Brava's coast road between Sant Feliu de Guíxols and Tossa. Expect fast group rides, excellent coffee, and roads whose surface quality is consistently better than anything else in this collection.
